title: Cheat Sheet - Instructions
markdown:
Intel syntax, NASM: the destination comes first. `r` is a register, `m` memory, `imm` a constant.

## Registers

| 64 | 32 | 16 | 8 | System V role |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rax` | `eax` | `ax` | `al` | result; system call number |
| `rbx` | `ebx` | `bx` | `bl` | kept by calls |
| `rcx` | `ecx` | `cx` | `cl` | 4th argument; shift count |
| `rdx` | `edx` | `dx` | `dl` | 3rd argument; high half of mul and div |
| `rsi` | `esi` | `si` | `sil` | 2nd argument |
| `rdi` | `edi` | `di` | `dil` | 1st argument |
| `rbp` | `ebp` | `bp` | `bpl` | kept by calls; frame base |
| `rsp` | `esp` | `sp` | `spl` | stack pointer |
| `r8`, `r9` | `r8d` | `r8w` | `r8b` | 5th, 6th arguments |
| `r10`, `r11` | | | | scratch (`syscall` changes `r11` and `rcx`) |
| `r12` to `r15` | `r12d` | `r12w` | `r12b` | kept by calls |

Writing a 32-bit register zeroes the upper 32 bits; writing 8 or 16 bits leaves the rest.

## Moving data

| Instruction | Does |
|---|---|
| `mov r, r/m/imm` · `mov m, r/imm` | copy |
| `movzx r, byte/word m` | widen with 0s |
| `movsx r, byte/word m` · `movsxd r64, dword m` | widen with the sign |
| `lea r, [address]` | compute an address (or arithmetic) without reading memory |
| `xchg a, b` | swap |
| `push r/imm` · `pop r` | the stack: rsp −8 then store · load then rsp +8 |
| `cmovcc r, r/m` | copy if the condition holds |
| `setcc r8` | 1 or 0 by the condition |

## Arithmetic and logic

| Instruction | Does | Flags |
|---|---|---|
| `add` · `sub` | a ± b | all |
| `adc` · `sbb` | with the carry | all |
| `inc` · `dec` | ± 1 | all but CF |
| `neg` | −a | all |
| `imul r, r/m` · `imul r, r/m, imm` | low 64 bits of a product | CF, OF |
| `mul r/m` · `imul r/m` | `rdx:rax` = `rax` × operand | CF, OF |
| `div r/m` · `idiv r/m` | `rdx:rax` ÷ operand: quotient `rax`, remainder `rdx` (prepare `rdx` with `xor edx, edx` or `cqo`) | |
| `and` · `or` · `xor` · `not` | bitwise | (not: none) |
| `shl` · `shr` · `sar` · `rol` · `ror` | shifts and rotates, by imm or `cl` | |
| `cmp a, b` | a − b, flags only | all |
| `test a, b` | a AND b, flags only | all |
| `popcnt r, r/m` | count the 1 bits | |
| `bt` · `bts` · `btr` · `btc` | test, set, clear, flip one bit | CF |

## Jumps and calls

| Instruction | Does |
|---|---|
| `jmp label` · `jmp [m]` | always (directly or through a table) |
| `je`/`jz` · `jne`/`jnz` | equal / not equal |
| `jl` · `jle` · `jg` · `jge` | signed comparisons |
| `jb` · `jbe` · `ja` · `jae` | unsigned comparisons |
| `js` · `jns` · `jo` · `jc` | sign, overflow, carry |
| `call label` | push the return address, jump |
| `ret` | pop the return address into rip |
| `syscall` | ask the kernel: number in `rax`, arguments `rdi`, `rsi`, `rdx`, `r10`, `r8`, `r9` |

## Memory

```
[ base + index*scale + displacement ]     scale = 1, 2, 4 or 8
[rel label]                               relative to rip
byte / word / dword / qword [ ... ]       1, 2, 4, 8 bytes
```

String instructions, repeated `rcx` times with `rep`: `movsb` (copy `[rsi]` to `[rdi]`), `stosb` (store `al` at `[rdi]`).

## SIMD (SSE2, 128-bit xmm0 to xmm15)

`movdqu xmm, m` · `movdqu m, xmm` · `pxor` · `paddb`/`paddw`/`paddd`/`paddq` · `psubd` · `paddusb` (saturating) · `pcmpeqb` · `pminub` · `pmaxub` · `pshufd xmm, xmm, imm` · `movq r64, xmm`

## Data and sections

```nasm-norun
        section .data           ; data with starting values
x:      dq      42              ; db 1 byte, dw 2, dd 4, dq 8
s:      db      "text", 10, 0
n       equ     $ - s           ; a constant: the bytes since s
        times 8 db 0            ; repeat
        section .rodata         ; read-only data
        section .bss            ; zeroed space
buf:    resb    256             ; resw, resd, resq
        section .text           ; code
        global  _start
_start:
```

## System calls (Linux x86-64)

| `rax` | Call | Arguments |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | read | `rdi` = file, `rsi` = buffer, `rdx` = most bytes |
| 1 | write | `rdi` = file, `rsi` = bytes, `rdx` = how many |
| 60 | exit | `rdi` = exit code |

Files: 0 standard input, 1 standard output, 2 standard error. A failing call returns −error in `rax`.
